Project scope: The Powerhouse Ultimo Renewal (PUR) project vision is to see Powerhouse Ultimo focus on design and fashion, presenting exhibitions that showcase the museums significant collections, international exclusive exhibitions and programs that support the design and fashion industries. The renewal will deliver expanded and refurbished exhibition and public space, connecting Powerhouse Ultimo to the Sydney CBD by re-orienting the museum to the Goods Line and adjacent dining, entertaining and cultural precincts. A design competition is currently underway, led by Create NSW, with the successful scheme to be awarded in December 2022. The PUR project is being delivered by Infrastructure NSW on behalf of Powerhouse and Create. The delivery includes completion of a Stage 2 State Significant Development Application (SSDA) along with the preparation of tender documentation for a contractor to construct the project. This request is to engage a mechanical and electrical services provider to support the development of the PUR project. The delivery includes completion of the following stages of the project: Development of Concept Design; Schematic Design; SSDA documentation; Design Development; Tender Documentation; Contractor Procurement; Design Development Completion; Construction Documentation; Construction Phase Services; and Defect Liability Period Services.

Project scope: The NSW Government is funding the ALC initiative under the Closing the Gap (CTG) Priority Reforms that are set out in the NSW Closing the Gap Implementation Plan 2022-2024. The objective of Aboriginal-led commissioning is to drive an approach to commissioning that gives Aboriginal communities decision making power when it comes to the design, delivery and monitoring of programs and services, and ensures that they: build on the strengths of communities are culturally embedded, and are responsive to opportunities and needs that communities identify themselves. Driven by principles of self-determination and accountability, the ALC initiative will ensure that solutions are owned by Aboriginal communities and place Aboriginal culture as a key driver in service design. The ALC initiative aims to deliver outcomes for Aboriginal people and communities that are defined and driven by Aboriginal people and communities. The ALC initiative will be led by an Aboriginal Controlled Community Organisation (ACC), that will design and trial an approach to Aboriginal-led commissioning over two phases: Phase 1: establish a project team to carry out strategy, design and planning for implementation of a model for Aboriginal-led commissioning. Phase 2: trial the implementation of the model by commissioning service delivery initiatives in trial sites identified in partnership with a cross-agency steering committee.

Project Overview The WPCA is tasked with the design and delivery of the Bradfield City Centre – creating a dynamic new place for people to live, work and learn. The Bradfield City Centre comprises a total land area of 114.9ha of land located at 215 Badgery’s Creek Road. The first phase of creation involves the delivery of approximately 20 hectares in the western portion of the site. Concurrent Engagements As part of the first phase of City creation, several concurrent activities are occurring involving a number of consultants that have been engaged or are in the process of being engaged. The main engagement that the Sewer Pump Station and Stormwater Infrastructure Consultant will interface with is the First Stage Enabling Works Head Consultant. The First Stage Enabling Works Head Consultant will provide the following services: • Civil Works: Site gradings, earthworks, road pavements, piped and open stormwater drainage and coordination with streetscape landscaping. • Water Utilities: Potable and recycled water reticulation mains, and stormwater network for non-potable water uses. • Digital Smart City: Providing for all the digital plumbing including pits and pipes, smart poles and connections to the future communication data centres • Electrical Utilities: Providing for all the electrical reticulation network to service the wider precincts with Bradfield City Centre. • Waste: Design of a dedicated organic food collection pressure pipe system and collection tank for all the organic food waste to enable waste to energy opportunities. The collection tank will connect to the sewer pump station for overflow discharge. Services under this Engagement The following design work and construction phase services are envisaged to be managed and delivered by the consultant: • Stormwater Design: detailed modelling for all aspects of precinct wide stormwater quality and quantity to allow the concept design of the stormwater management strategy infrastructure for the entire Bradfield City Centre. Detailed design of Parkland West aspects of the stormwater infrastructure along Moore Gully. Detailed design of Parkland East aspects of the stormwater infrastructure along Thompson Creek. • Technical Advice: provision of technical advice and design solutions for options (allow consideration of 2 options) for servicing Bradfield City Centre’s recycled water demand from utilising on-site stormwater.

Project scope: Deliverables Description Detailed project plan The detailed project plan should include information such as key timings and milestones, risks and mitigation, review and feedback of draft content by the Department, evaluation process and preparation of the final data report. Redevelopment of the Existing Course and receipt of the Modified Training Course The Department seeks engaging and practical sector resources accessible to targeted educators and staff, that provide key regulatory quality and safety information and guidance. The Department welcomes innovative ideas Red Nose might have about engaging language, content and interactivity. Any additional content and included materials are to be sourced from reputable sources, expert industry specialists and/or accredited by a relevant sector expert such as NSW government departments or ACECQA. The purpose of the redevelopment is to bring the Existing Course in line with the October sleep regulation changes (84A-D) to create the Modified Training Course. The Department is to provide Red Nose with an extracted version of the Existing Course, with suggested changes as a starting point for amendments. This will consider any video content that contains names, logos or any identifying imagery of current services or providers being removed. Any key information included in the video to be included in another manner, such as text based interactive content or other. Red Nose will develop the Modified Training Course to be hosted on Red Noses LMS platform. As part of the existing format of the nine modules, the following concepts must be included: 1. Division 1A Sleep regulation changes (October 2023); 2. Supervision - sleeping/resting children always being in sight and hearing distance of an educator; 3. Supervision - physical checks of sleeping/resting children; 4. Safe equipment; 5. Safe environment; and 6. Effective risk assessments, policies and procedures for safe sleep. The completion certificate is to be amended to include the completion date and distinguish between Red Nose's Existing Course and the Department's funded enrolments into the Modified Training Course. Red Nose must provide draft content to the Departments project team for review and feedback. Red Nose must work with the project team to address feedback and suggested amendments and allow adequate time for this to occur. Timelines for review and feedback will be determined between the Department and Red Nose and may be subject to change. Send draft built modules for review by the Department (noting content will have been approved by the Department already). The relevant Department executive must approve the final content prior to delivery. The Modified Training Course should be culturally responsive and support Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander providers in participation and engagement. The target audience for the Modified Training Course will be all early childhood education and care sector staff, including approved providers, service leaders and educators. Content must consider the targeted audience with reflection of educational level, learning needs, knowledge and experience of the targeted audience. Red Nose should develop the Modified Training Course to be inclusive and consider continued accessibility for participants. The Modified Training Course must consider the departments accessibility guidelines, specifically, the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.0. This includes registration questions, explicit consent for data sharing between Red Nose and the Department in the form agreed in writing between the parties and pre and post feedback surveys using the Department's evaluation framework. Product As specified in Schedule 4, and requirements as specified under the heading Modified Training Course (2200 tokens issued)'. Project scope: The works include re-sheeting sections of 70km Trail within the Carrai, Willi Willi and Werrikimbe National Parks and in particular Coachwood and Carrai Roads. Gravel sheeting is required to improve traction and reduce slippage, after reshaping the carriageway surface. This process involves adding a layer of gravel, typically around 150mm thick, to the existing surface to create a more stable and less slippery riding surface. Gravel re-sheeting typically involves loosening the existing surface (e.g., with a tyning machine) to ensure proper bonding with the new gravel layer. A layer of new gravel is then spread evenly across the surface. Finally, the gravel is compacted to create a solid, stable surface. The works may also include clearing regrowth and vegetation, repairing trail surfaces, clearing drainage structures and culvert cleaning and repairs. This engagement will involve the provision of various plant and equipment items, each with qualified operators, under a wet hire arrangement. Prepare a Geotechnical Investigation Report that details the methodology, test results and findings from the geotechnical site investigations. 9. Undertake design development of remediation works to inform the development of a detailed design that is construct only except for the Southern waste rock cut quantities and fill for the open pits. 10. The outcomes will result in substantial changes to Lismore, with significant areas of previously residential land being converted to other land uses and zones. The Lismore community is still recovering from the 2022 floods, and this project is an opportunity to develop a positive vision for the future through meaningful collaboration with the community and other stakeholders.

Slickline services will be required throughout the well testing duration to open and/or close SSDs accordingly as required to flow test each zone of interest.
